description: Century Egg Congee, also known as Pidan Congee, is a classic Chinese comfort food perfect for breakfast or a light meal. This savory rice porridge is simmered to a silky smooth consistency, often with shredded pork, and features the unique, earthy flavor of century eggs. Garnished with fresh ginger and green onions, it offers a deeply satisfying and traditional taste experience.

instructions.title: Prepare the Rice
instructions.text: Wash the jasmine rice thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. For extra smooth congee, soak the washed rice in 2 cups of water with a pinch of salt and a teaspoon of cooking oil for at least 30 minutes, or even overnight. This helps the rice grains break down faster.

instructions.title: Marinate the Pork
instructions.text: Shred the pork loin into thin strips. In a bowl, combine the shredded pork with 1 teaspoon cornstarch, 1 teaspoon soy sauce, 1/2 teaspoon Shaoxing wine, and a pinch of white pepper. Mix well and set aside to marinate for at least 15 minutes.

instructions.title: Prepare Century Eggs and Aromatics
instructions.text: Peel the century eggs and cut them into small, bite-sized wedges or cubes. Peel and slice the fresh ginger, then julienne half of it for garnish and leave the other half sliced for cooking. Chop the green onions, separating the white parts from the green parts.

instructions.title: Start the Congee Base
instructions.text: In a large pot, combine the soaked rice (including the soaking water if any), 8-10 cups of water or chicken broth, and the sliced ginger. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for at least 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking. The goal is for the rice grains to break down and form a creamy, thick porridge.

instructions.title: Add Pork and Century Eggs
instructions.text: Once the congee has reached a thick, creamy consistency and the rice grains have burst, increase the heat to medium-low. Add the marinated pork strips, stirring gently to separate them. Cook for 3-5 minutes until the pork is cooked through. Then, add most of the cut century eggs, reserving some for garnish. Stir to combine.

instructions.title: Season and Serve
instructions.text: Season the congee with salt and white pepper to taste. Stir in the white parts of the chopped green onions. Ladle the hot congee into individual serving bowls. Garnish with the reserved julienned ginger, remaining century egg pieces, and the green parts of the chopped green onions. A drizzle of sesame oil is optional for added aroma. Serve immediately.

tips: For an extra smooth and creamy congee, freeze the washed rice overnight before cooking. The freezing process breaks down the rice grains, allowing them to burst open more easily during simmering, resulting in a silkier texture.
When selecting century eggs, look for those with firm, dark yolks and jelly-like whites. For a milder flavor, you can briefly rinse the peeled century eggs under cold water before dicing.

Congee tends to thicken significantly upon cooling. When reheating leftover congee, you may need to add a little water or broth to achieve the desired consistency. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2-3 days.
article:
Discover the ultimate comfort food and a cornerstone of Chinese breakfast cuisine: Congee with Century Egg. This savory rice porridge, known as Pidan Shou Rou Zhou (皮蛋瘦肉粥) in Cantonese, is a beloved dish cherished for its silky texture, rich umami flavor, and satisfying warmth. Perfect for a chilly morning or a soothing meal when you need something light yet flavorful, Century Egg Congee offers a unique culinary experience that’s both traditional and deeply comforting. If you’ve ever wondered how to recreate this iconic dish at home, you’re in the right place. Get ready to dive into the world of authentic Chinese breakfast recipes and master this creamy, flavorful porridge.

## What is Century Egg Congee?
At its heart, Century Egg Congee is a comforting bowl of rice porridge, slow-cooked until the grains break down into a velvety, creamy consistency. What elevates it from a simple porridge to a culinary masterpiece are two key ingredients: century eggs and lean pork.

Century eggs (also known as preserved eggs or pidan) are a traditional Chinese delicacy made by preserving duck, chicken, or quail eggs in a mixture of clay, ash, salt, quicklime, and rice hulls for several weeks or months. The preservation process transforms the egg white into a translucent, dark amber jelly with a slightly salty and savory taste, while the yolk becomes a dark green, creamy, and pungent paste. Don't be intimidated by their appearance or unique aroma; when diced and incorporated into the congee, they lend an incredible depth of umami and a distinctive, slightly earthy flavor that is surprisingly harmonious.

The lean pork, typically shredded or minced, adds another layer of savoriness and a tender texture to the porridge. Combined with fragrant ginger, green onions, and sometimes a hint of white pepper and sesame oil, the Century Egg Congee becomes a symphony of textures and flavors – creamy, savory, slightly pungent, and utterly delicious. It's a truly iconic Chinese breakfast, perfect for starting the day with warmth and nourishment.

## Ingredients You Need
Crafting the perfect Century Egg Congee requires a few essential ingredients. Here’s what you’ll need to gather:

*   **For the Congee Base:**
    *   1 cup long-grain white rice (Jasmine rice works beautifully for its fragrance)
    *   8-10 cups water or chicken/pork broth (broth adds significant flavor)
    *   1-inch piece of ginger, peeled and thinly sliced or smashed
    *   1/2 teaspoon salt (or to taste)
    *   1/4 teaspoon white pepper (or to taste)
    *   1 teaspoon sesame oil (optional, for drizzling at the end)

*   **For the Century Egg & Pork Component:**
    *   2-3 century eggs, peeled and diced into small pieces
    *   6-8 ounces lean pork loin or pork shoulder, thinly sliced or minced
    *   1 tablespoon soy sauce (for marinating pork)
    *   1 teaspoon cornstarch (for marinating pork)
    *   1 tablespoon cooking oil (e.g., vegetable or canola oil)
    *   2-3 scallions (green onions), chopped for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions
Making Century Egg Congee is more about patience than complex techniques. Follow these steps for a perfect bowl:

1.  **Prepare the Rice:** Rinse the rice thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear. For an extra creamy congee, you can soak the rice in water for at least 30 minutes, or even overnight, before cooking. This helps the grains break down faster. Some also recommend freezing the rice overnight after washing; the ice crystals help shatter the grains when cooked.

2.  **Marinate the Pork:** While the rice is soaking, prepare your pork. Slice or mince the lean pork and place it in a bowl. Add the soy sauce and cornstarch, mixing well until the pork is evenly coated. Set aside to marinate for at least 15 minutes. The cornstarch helps tenderize the pork and keeps it moist.

3.  **Start the Congee Base:** In a large pot (a heavy-bottomed pot is ideal to prevent sticking), combine the rinsed rice, water or broth, and sliced ginger. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil over high heat.

4.  **Simmer and Stir:** Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot partially (leaving a small gap for steam to escape), and let it simmer. Stir the congee every 15-20 minutes to prevent the rice from sticking to the bottom of the pot and to encourage an even breakdown of the grains. Continue simmering for at least 1.5 to 2 hours, or until the rice grains have burst open and the congee has reached a thick, creamy, porridge-like consistency. If it becomes too thick, add a little more hot water or broth.

5.  **Cook the Pork and Add Century Eggs:** About 20-30 minutes before the congee is ready, heat a tablespoon of cooking oil in a separate pan over medium-high heat. Add the marinated pork and stir-fry until it's just cooked through and no longer pink. Remove from heat. Gently fold the cooked pork and the diced century eggs into the simmering congee.

6.  **Season and Serve:** Continue to simmer for another 10-15 minutes to allow the flavors to meld. Stir in the salt and white pepper. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed. Ladle the hot Century Egg Congee into bowls, garnish generously with fresh chopped scallions, and drizzle with a touch of sesame oil if desired.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results
Achieving that perfect, silky smooth Century Egg Congee isn't hard, but a few tricks can elevate your dish:

*   **Rice-to-Water Ratio:** The general rule is 1 cup of rice to 8-10 cups of liquid for a thick congee. Adjust based on your preferred consistency. Less liquid for a thicker porridge, more for a thinner one.
*   **Use Broth:** While water works, using chicken or pork broth will significantly enhance the depth of flavor in your congee. It adds a savory foundation that water alone can't provide.
*   **Constant Stirring (but not too much):** Regular stirring is crucial to prevent sticking and encourage creaminess, but you don't need to stand over it constantly. Every 15-20 minutes is usually sufficient.
*   **Don't Rush It:** True congee takes time. The slow simmer is what breaks down the rice grains and creates that signature velvety texture. Plan for at least 1.5 to 2 hours of cooking time.
*   **Marinate the Pork:** This step is essential for tender, flavorful pork. The cornstarch creates a protective coating that keeps the meat moist during cooking.
*   **Add Century Egg Towards the End:** Adding the century eggs too early might cause them to break down too much. Adding them in the last 15-20 minutes allows them to warm through and integrate their flavor without disappearing entirely.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** Always taste your congee before serving and adjust salt, pepper, or even a dash of soy sauce to your liking.

## Serving Suggestions
Century Egg Congee is a meal in itself, but it truly shines when paired with traditional Chinese accompaniments.

*   **Youtiao (Chinese Fried Dough Sticks):** These crispy, savory fried dough sticks are the quintessential companion. Tear them into pieces and dip them into the hot congee for a delightful contrast in texture.
*   **Pickled Vegetables:** A small side of pickled radish, cucumber, or mustard greens offers a refreshing tang that cuts through the richness of the congee.
*   **Extra Seasonings:** Offer small bowls of soy sauce, white pepper, or even chili oil on the side, allowing diners to customize their bowl to their preference.
*   **Fresh Herbs:** A sprinkle of fresh cilantro or more chopped scallions can brighten the dish with their aromatic freshness.
*   **Peanuts or Fried Shallots:** For an added crunch and burst of flavor, consider sprinkling some roasted peanuts or crispy fried shallots on top.

## Variations and Substitutions
While Century Egg Congee is a classic, don't hesitate to experiment and make it your own!

*   **Different Meats:** Instead of lean pork, try shredded chicken (a great way to use leftover rotisserie chicken), thinly sliced beef, or even delicate white fish fillets. For chicken, you can poach chicken breast and shred it, adding it in the last 15 minutes of cooking.
*   **Vegetarian Options:** Omit the pork and use a mushroom-based broth. Add thinly sliced mushrooms (shiitake or oyster mushrooms work well) or silken tofu for extra texture and protein.
*   **Other Preserved Eggs:** While century egg is distinctive, some recipes also incorporate salted duck eggs, which offer a different salty, rich flavor. You can even use both for a "double egg" congee!
*   **Add Vegetables:** Towards the end of cooking, stir in some finely diced carrots, spinach, or bok choy for added nutrients and color.
*   **Flavor Boosters:** A dash of Shaoxing wine (Chinese cooking wine) can be added with the pork for an extra layer of complexity.

Whether you're a seasoned fan or a curious newcomer, making Century Egg Congee at home is a rewarding culinary journey. This comforting, flavorful, and deeply satisfying Chinese breakfast recipe is more than just food; it's a taste of tradition and a warm hug in a bowl. Enjoy the process of creating this classic dish, and savor every spoonful of your homemade Century Egg Congee.
